summary: The note explains how Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) are using the Internet of Things (IoT) to improve supply chain management through real-time tracking, inventory control, predictive maintenance, automated reordering, and better customer experience. It cites adoption statistics and quotes from specialists and business leaders, and discusses compliance benefits, challenges such as affordability and security, and the role of data analytics. It concludes that IoT will become a strategic asset enabling new business models for SMEs.
one_line: IoT gives SMEs affordable real-time tracking, inventory, maintenance, and analytics tools that transform supply chain management despite cost and security challenges.
key_facts: On November 10, 2023, at the Global SME Tech Summit, IoT specialist Maria Gonzalez said IoT devices provide real-time data and analytics so SMEs can make informed decisions swiftly, reducing waste and improving efficiency.
A report by the SME Innovation Institute, released by October 2023, found IoT adoption in SME supply chain management spiked by 37% compared to the previous year.
IoT devices in supply chains range from RFID tags to sensors on equipment or products.
James O'Conner has used IoT in his warehouse operations since September 15, 2023, and reports a 25% reduction in overstock situations using smart shelves and bins with weight sensors.

Grace Lee, Supply Chain Manager at GreenTech Innovations, said on December 1, 2023 that downtime decreased by 40% after integrating IoT into asset management, allowing maintenance only when necessary.
GreenTech Innovations is an SME specializing in renewable energy equipment.
FastLane Logistics has used IoT since September 2023 to give customers real-time order tracking; CEO Roberto Garcia says it has dramatically increased customer satisfaction.
IoT systems can autonomously place orders when inventory falls below predefined thresholds, saving time and preventing manual errors.
IoT traceability helps SMEs address compliance issues quickly, which is especially valuable in the food and pharmaceutical industries.
The main hurdles for SMEs adopting IoT are affordability, technological literacy, and security concerns.

On September 18, 2023, Mark Thompson of TechAdvisors started offering tailored IoT solutions to SMEs, saying the technology is now accessible and affordable and that proper protocols minimize data breach risk.
Advanced analytics on IoT data can forecast demand more accurately and optimize logistics routes.
The note anticipates IoT in 2024 and beyond becoming a strategic asset leading to new business models and revenue streams for SMEs.
